ad_rate.assumption: REVISED per critic finding K1: the prior base of 0.42 treated the year as calendar-month-flat, which double-counts the low-volume launch months. A blended ACoS must be volume-weighted, and this run's own forecast ramp is already backloaded (monthly_units_m6 base 70, monthly_units_m12 base 140, annual_units_y1 base ~1000 built from a ramp, not a flat average - see forecast section). Reconstructing that ramp: months 1-3 innovator-only at ~25 units/mo (~75 total, moore.chasm, no reviews yet, ACoS ~70% per the knowledge base's 40-80% launch band), months 4-6 ramping 40/55/70 units/mo (~165 total, ACoS tapering ~50% as first reviews land), months 7-9 ramping ~82/93/105 units/mo (~280 total, ACoS ~30% approaching the chasm-crossing point), months 10-12 ~140-160 units/mo with the Q4 bump (~450 total, ACoS ~20%, knowledge base's 15-30% steady-state band). Unit-weighting those four buckets (75/165/280/450 units at ~70%/50%/30%/20% ACoS) gives a blended base of ~32%, not 42% - the prior figure effectively over-weighted the thin early months. Low (0.18) reflects a faster-than-median chasm crossing (I1/I2's above-median thumbnail visibility per innovaty landing CTR/conversion ahead of schedule) pushing more of the year into the steady-state low end; high (0.55) reflects the pre-mortem's 'review velocity never crossed the chasm' obituary (probability 0.30) where launch-heavy spend must be sustained well past month 6, dragging the annual blend up without ever reaching the full 40-80% launch-only ceiling for a whole year.

forecast.seasonality_note: Q4 (November-December) carries a modest general Amazon gift/replacement bump for pet accessories; back-to-school (August) and January 'organize my life' demand spikes named in the knowledge base do not apply meaningfully to this specific product category.
forecast.reasoning: Outside in: scout could not source a direct top-10-20-ASIN monthly unit total for this term (a real gap), so genius built a reasoned 1,200-2,800 (base 2,000) combined monthly-unit estimate from indirect signals (F1's 6+ named competing SKUs, F6's 73-review long-lived listing) and marked it stale. Multiplying share by term volume gives 24-168 units/month at month 6 and 48-308 at month 12; a month-by-month ramp (not a flat multiply-by-12) that weights months 1-3 lightly and adds a small Q4 bump produces the 300-1,900 (base ~1,000) unit annual range.

three_sentences_to_founder: Ship v1_now (I2, I3, I4, I5) first and hold the clear see-through sift window (I1) for a fast-follow: it adds about $0.22 to base unit cost and triggers a mandatory prior-art search this launch doesn't need to fund yet, while v1_now's landed cost still runs about $4.44 on a roughly $18.99 base price - about 24% of price, comfortably inside the 30% rail.

The real threat to this 'FRAGILE MARGIN' product is advertising, not tooling: running this plan's own ranges through the contribution formula at the $18.99 base price and a corrected, volume-weighted year-one blended ACoS of 32% (down from an earlier, unweighted 42% that over-counted the low-volume launch months - see economics.ad_rate) gives per-unit contribution of about $1.60, roughly 8% of price - positive, not negative, but still below the 15%-of-price no-go floor, so on base-case numbers this plan does not clear the contribution sanity rail and feasibility is reclassified from 'stretch' to 'unrealistic' until ad efficiency, price or cost genuinely improve; review velocity (Vine plus the packaging insert card) is now a precondition for viability, not a nice-to-have.

Budget roughly $8,150-$32,200 in tooling and launch costs and 33-55 weeks to first sale (1.35x planning-fallacy buffer already applied), and treat the pin-gauge QC check on every production batch as the single highest-stakes step, since a widened mesh gauge is the exact failure mode the brief's own seller_constraints warns against.
